title: [US-1] Scheduled Identity & Access Telemetry
body:
**Story ID:** US-1
**Agent:** `auditor_agent` | **Framework:** Google ADK (`google-adk`)

As an IT Operations Manager, I want the system to automatically scan IdP logs every 24–72 hours and flag applications with zero activity or redundant capabilities, so I don't have to manually hunt for zombie systems.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] System connects to identity providers (Okta, Google Workspace, Azure AD) using Firebase Authentication (via OAuth 2.0 or SAML federation)
- [ ] Cron-based Auditor Agent executes on a configurable schedule (default: every 48 hours) triggered by Cloud Scheduler → Cloud Run
- [ ] Flags application when ≥60% of assigned seats show zero SAML/OIDC logins over 60+ days
- [ ] Detects capability redundancy using Gemini Flash for semantic tag matching
- [ ] Generates structured JSON payload stored in Firestore
- [ ] Logs all detection logic to Cloud Audit Logs for forensic reconstruction

title: [US-2] Expense & Webhook Ingestion

title: [US-3] Auditor Agent Consolidation Proposal Generation
body:
**Story ID:** US-3
**Agent:** `auditor_agent` | **Framework:** Google ADK (`google-adk`) | **Model:** Gemini Pro

As an IT Ops Manager, I want the system to create a detailed, human-readable consolidation proposal before any migration begins, so I understand what's at risk and can make an informed decision.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Auditor Agent generates structured JSON payload with redundant application identifier, target enterprise standard, and estimated annual savings
- [ ] Calculates savings as: seats × cost per seat × months remaining (Cloud SQL billing data)
- [ ] Generates risk score (0–100) using Gemini Pro reasoning based on active user count, connected integrations, data age, compliance sensitivity
- [ ] Summarizes detected dependencies (Zapier webhooks, custom fields, automation rules)
- [ ] Provides recommendation: Proceed to Full Consolidation, Proceed with Manual Review, or Ignore/Whitelist
- [ ] Proposal is timestamped and signed for audit trail, stored in Firestore

## ADK Agent Architecture
```python
# Capstone tools for auditor_agent (uses Gemini Pro)
def generate_proposal(app_id: str) -> dict: ...
def calculate_roi(app_id: str) -> dict: ...
```

title: [US-5] 3-Tier HITL Approval Gates
body:
**Story ID:** US-5
**Agent:** Root Orchestrator (`zombie_saas_coordinator`) | **Framework:** Google ADK (`google-adk`)

As a CISO, I want distinct, mandatory human approval gates for investigation, migration, and destruction (data migration, account revocation, subscription cancellation), so we maintain accountability and can halt the process if new information emerges.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] System enforces three distinct authorization gates: Permission to Investigate, Permission to Migrate, Permission to Dispose
- [ ] Root orchestrator does NOT delegate to Architect/Integrator agents without explicit human approval
- [ ] Approval is tied to authenticated SSO identity verified via Firebase Authentication (not a generic API token)
- [ ] Approval expires after 7 days; re-issue required if migration not completed within window
- [ ] System can be halted at any stage if IT Ops or CISO revokes approval
- [ ] All halts logged with reason and authorizing identity

## ADK Agent Architecture
Implements **ADK Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) pattern** with `FirestoreSessionService`:
```python
from google.adk.sessions import FirestoreSessionService

session_service = FirestoreSessionService(
    project_id="zombie-saas-coordinator",
    collection="agent_sessions",
)

def check_approval_status(proposal_id: str) -> dict: ...
def revoke_approval(proposal_id: str, reason: str) -> dict: ...
```

title: [US-6] Behavioral Contract Extraction
body:
**Story ID:** US-6
**Agent:** `architect_agent` | **Framework:** Google ADK (`google-adk`) | **Model:** Gemini Pro

As a Technical Lead, I want the system to automatically extract automation rules and behavioral logic from the source system (Trello) so we can verify that the target system (Asana) can enforce the same rules after migration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Architect Agent connects to Trello API and parses all board configurations
- [ ] Extracts automation and Power-Up rules in structured format (trigger, action, scope)
- [ ] Records trigger conditions (status change, label addition, etc.) and actions (archive, move, notify)
- [ ] Records custom fields, due dates, card labels, and checklists
- [ ] Exports behavioral contract as JSON specification document stored in Firestore
- [ ] Logs all API calls and extracted rules to Cloud Audit Logs

## ADK Agent Architecture
```python
from google.adk.agents import Agent

def extract_trello_rules(board_id: str) -> dict: ...
def parse_automation_rule(raw_rule: dict) -> dict: ...

architect_agent = Agent(
    name="architect_agent",
    model="gemini-2.0-pro",
    description="Validates semantic compatibility between source and target SaaS platforms",
    tools=[extract_trello_rules, parse_automation_rule],
)
```

title: [US-10] Automation Hub Scanning
body:
**Story ID:** US-10
**Agent:** `integrator_agent` | **Framework:** Google ADK (`google-adk`) | **Model:** Gemini Flash

As an IT Ops Manager, I want the system to automatically find all Zapier and Make workflows that depend on the Trello integration, so we know which automations will break if we decommission Trello.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Integrator Agent connects to Zapier API and Make API via OAuth 2.0
- [ ] Queries for all active zaps/workflows containing Trello as trigger or action
- [ ] For each workflow, records: workflow name, trigger condition, action, downstream dependencies
- [ ] Identifies critical workflows (e.g., daily syncs, customer-facing automations)
- [ ] Generates dependency graph stored in Firestore showing Trello → Zapier/Make → other SaaS tools
- [ ] Flags workflows that will break if Trello is decommissioned
- [ ] All API calls and dependencies logged to Cloud Audit Logs

## ADK Agent Architecture
```python
from google.adk.agents import Agent

def scan_zapier(app_name: str) -> dict: ...
def scan_make(app_name: str) -> dict: ...
def build_dependency_graph(workflows: list[dict]) -> dict: ...

integrator_agent = Agent(
    name="integrator_agent",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description="Scans automation hubs for workflow dependencies",
    tools=[scan_zapier, scan_make, build_dependency_graph],
)
```
Runs in **parallel** with Architect Agent pipeline (US-6→US-9) after HITL gate.

title: [US-11] Migration Execution & Reconciliation
body:
**Story ID:** US-11
**Agent:** orchestrator_agent | **Framework:** Google ADK

As a Compliance Officer, I want cryptographic proof that the migrated data matches the source data before we approve cutover, so I am confident no data was lost.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] System generates a migration manifest and source-to-target ID mapping during the MIGRATING phase.
- [ ] RECONCILING phase checks paginated extraction counts, verifies attachments/comments, and executes field-level checks.
- [ ] Outputs a post-migration exception report for isolated failures.

title: [US-12] Fail-Safe Quarantine and Disposal
body:
**Story ID:** US-12
**Agent:** orchestrator_agent | **Framework:** Google ADK

As a CISO, I want source data quarantined by default and destroyed only after a separate, explicit authorization to ensure compliance with data retention policies.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Default action after migration is SOURCE_QUARANTINED (retention of source data).
- [ ] Disposal is blocked if validation exceptions, legal holds, or incomplete migrations remain unresolved.
- [ ] Requires a separate, multi-signature approval (DISPOSAL_APPROVED) before verifiable destruction.
